set.body:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 2 Scoring channel.

Every score producer (lexical, embedding, later language models) feeds the decoder through one typed score interface, separate from the label-producing interface. Related: bd-01M16TYAMC8TA58V0TW6CJET6Y found empty-input guards with opposite, undeclared conventions in the cost model.

Scope:
The interface, the lexical and embedding providers, and replay.

Acceptance criteria:
1. One typed score interface with a receipt per call.
2. It declares its candidate level (scene or leaf) and the rule distributing scene scores over leaves for GraphHsmm; the docs state that a scene-level score alone cannot establish within-scene precision.
3. A recorded-response replay mode lets every gate run with no model and no network.
4. Lexical and embedding providers exist; an unavailable score is a typed outcome, never zero or uniform (test).
5. Each provider declares its empty-input class (forced / conservative / flattering) per bd-01M16TYAMC8TA58V0TW6CJET6Y; no flattering default reaches the decoder (test).
6. Parity: the embedding provider's Sherlock emissions are byte-identical to the current pipeline's when serialized (or within a stated tolerance, justified in the commit).

Gate (AGENTS.md SD2/SD6): `sbt -batch clean compileAll testAll` on the merge result, then
`sbt -batch scalafmtCheckAll scalafmtSbtCheck` as a separate run; every test task in build.sbt's
testAll alias reports bound totals (56 at 0e36a7fa, after the corpus modules were added; recount if
modules change); a named mutation witness per new guard, and each compile-time-probe mutation proved
after its own clean recompile; `cd docs-site && npm run verify:examples` when public API or examples
change; fresh-context cold review in a separate pass; the commit body states the evidence and what
it does not establish.

Size: M.
set.title: Phase 2: typed scoring-channel interface with receipts and recorded-response replay
